Every citation on a mover, volume outlier, or recommendation card carries the actual publish date of its source, separate from this page's pull date above. Price/volume/index data always refreshes live on pull; narrative research is only rewritten when genuinely newer reporting was found for that name - otherwise the existing writeup stands rather than being re-presented under a fresher-looking timestamp. The 10/18/26 pull (a Sunday) reflects the Friday Oct 16 session - equity data is current through that close, with no data lag. It was a sharp two-way day: the Nasdaq fell 2.15% (-4.5% on the week, its worst since late June) as an eight-session chip losing streak, a software selloff and stress in AI-linked debt (CoreWeave -12%) hit semis, semicap, AI-infrastructure, AI-pivoting bitcoin miners and software names - so the 10/18/26 pull's losers (Vicor, Supermicro, Flex, Impinj, Ultra Clean, ACM Research, MaxLinear, Viavi, DigitalOcean, Twilio, Okta, Five9, MARA, CleanSpark, Centrus) are mostly one sector-wide story, not 15 separate ones. Several of these names already had September writeups about earlier, opposite-direction moves; those are kept as 'Prior framing' under a dated UPDATE rather than overwritten. Supermicro is the main name with genuinely new company-specific news (an Oct 8-9 guilty plea in a server-diversion case that reopens a question the prior writeup called cleared). Gainers were almost entirely oil and gas: Brent settled near $110 (highest since May) and WTI near $101 on Iran's escalating Hormuz attacks and a large US crude draw, lifting E&Ps and midstream together. Most of those names had no company-specific catalyst and are marked as sector-beta reads; natural-gas futures actually fell that day, so gas-weighted names (Antero, Range) are marked divergent from their own commodity. Several volume outliers (Regions, Citizens, Alcoa, First Financial, Cohen & Steers) are earnings-driven; ten others (Schneider National, Sunstone, Urban Edge, DXP, Ormat, Avantor, Ecolab, Watts, Central Garden, Northern Trust) turned up no clean catalyst despite a genuine search - Oct 16 was a monthly options expiration, which commonly inflates volume, but that is stated as an unconfirmed explanation, not a sourced one. The $2B market-cap filter was refreshed on 10/18/26 (2026-10-18 cache), which moved Ichor and Schrodinger below the line and brought Flex and Impinj into the losers list; Flex's slide traces to the Oct 5 terms of a $2B convertible-preferred deal in its Axiom unit, while Impinj had no clean catalyst ahead of its Oct 28 earnings. Ciena joins the bounce list (sector de-rating after the Oct 1 optical rally reversed).

Crescent Energy jumped 10.1% on ~3x average volume on Oct 16, the biggest gain in a sector-wide oil rally: Brent settled at $109.86 (+3.7%, highest settle since May 19, briefly touching $110) and WTI Nov at $101.41 (+3.5%) on Fri Oct 16 on renewed Middle East supply fears, Russian-diesel uncertainty and an 8.6M-bbl US crude draw (week to Oct 9), while the broader tape fell (S&P -1.1%, Nasdaq -2.1%) on AI-spending worries - energy was the day's best sector. Coverage of the move ties it to the crude/energy-stock advance and gives no new Crescent-specific catalyst that day. Context: on Oct 8 Crescent agreed to buy Devon's Eagle Ford assets (~$3.85B net) and priced an 80M-share offering at $12.50 (plus a 12M-share option exercise) to fund it; Friday's close ($13.77) put the stock back above that offering price, which may have amplified the move (our read, not sourced). Q3 results are due Nov 3.
